pocket: THE DEFLECTION CHANGES THE SHAFT BEFORE THE BODY; RECOVERY MUST MOVE THE HANDS BEFORE IT CAN MOVE THE WEAPON HOME.

source.title: Grim Reaper — Sword Master — NES — Enemies & Bosses
observed: Whole exact raster was inspected in commissioned campaign evidence.
Upper pose families contain a distinct long tool channel whose envelope changes materially relative to much of the lower body/support silhouette.
Source page/evidence identifies the tool family as axe/poleaxe.
Static sheet position does not establish playback chronology.
inferred: All Strikes019 pose geometry, chronology, support ownership, force direction, grip migration, return-corridor causality, timing, and connectors.
The synthetic deflection event and hand-spacing recovery gate.
unknown: Exact source gameplay order, hitbox/contact point, source root trajectory, weapon mass, hit-stop duration, and source-authentic exposure spacing.

direction.thesis: An external deflection rotates the tool before the pelvis can repay forward momentum. The old grip spacing becomes mechanically wrong; a visible hand migration must occur before the hook can retract on its new axis and only then counterrotate home.
required_read: grip spacing visibly changes under load
retract on new deflected axis before counterrotation
torso overshoot plus distal shaft lag
displaced ready rather than idle reset

compile.connective_motion: deterministic linear geometry between authored keys; semantic events remain key-owned

keys.name: CROOKED_READY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Displaced asymmetric ready; tool task clock quiet.

keys.name: REAR_COIL
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Root shifts back; rear hip loads while distal hook keeps a readable return reserve.

keys.name: PELVIS_COMMIT
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Pelvis/root commits before the hook reaches the line.

keys.name: PRECONTACT_GAP
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Distinct air gap remains before the authored impact.

keys.name: DEFLECTION_CONTACT
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Contact is not maximum reach; external force begins rotating tool axis.

keys.name: ROOT_OVERRUN_TOOL_KICK
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Hook snaps up/back while pelvis/root continues forward one authored beat.

keys.name: NEAR_HAND_PIVOT_FAR_HAND_SLIDE
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Near hand becomes temporary pivot; far hand slides along shaft instead of dragging tool through old line.

keys.name: OUTER_SUPPORT_CATCH
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Wide front support catches returned torque; body compresses under the deflected axis.

keys.name: DEFLECTED_AXIS_LOAD_HOLD
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Tool and torso remain twisted; this hold makes the new return corridor legible.

keys.name: GRIP_MIGRATION
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Far hand migrates inward; hand spacing changes before major weapon recovery.

keys.name: NEW_AXIS_RETRACT
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Hook retracts along the deflected shaft axis; root does not rotate yet.

keys.name: HOOK_CLEAR
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Hook is now inside the legal return pocket; counterrotation becomes permissible.

keys.name: COUNTERROTATE_AFTER_CLEAR
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Hands rotate tool only after clearance; torso overshoots opposite the old deflection.

keys.name: SHAFT_LAG_SECONDARY_SETTLE
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Body has nearly restacked while distal shaft still lags right; no reverse interpolation.

keys.name: DISPLACED_READY
keys.motion_arc_root_note: Readiness returns at a new address and altered stance width; recovery does not reset to K00.

quality_iterations.defect: Grip migration was too visually subtle relative to the concept thesis; the diagonal tool kick read, but the hand-spacing transfer could be mistaken for ordinary recoil.
quality_iterations.correction: Strengthen SAME-body K06-K10: pin near-hand pivot, widen far-hand slide, deepen outer-support compression, then visibly collapse hand spacing before axial retract.

quality_iterations.basis: Actual 63-frame render: contact snaps the hooked head onto a new diagonal while pelvis continues forward; K06-K10 visibly change hand spacing under a deep front-support catch before new-axis retract; K11 clearance precedes K12 counterrotation; K13 preserves distal shaft lag into displaced K14.

The action has one readable nasty idea rather than decorative flourish: the deflection breaks the old grip solution, the body visibly pays for it, and recovery ends displaced rather than politely returning to neutral.

quality_iterations.defect: Premature K01 contact/deflection marker appeared during pre-persistence exact ASCII audit, before commitment and precontact gap.
quality_iterations.correction: SAME-body semantic fix: K01 contact_event=false and restore its intended rear-coil root note; preserve all geometry/timing.

quality_iterations.basis: Actual 63-frame render after semantic correction: clean rear coil without premature contact; K03 preserves gap; K04 contact rotates the tool; K05 root overruns; K06-K10 expose grip migration/support catch before new-axis retract; K11 clears; K12 counterrotates; K13 shaft lag survives into displaced K14.
The central joke is mechanical and visible: contact wrecks the old hand spacing, the fighter has to solve the hands before solving the weapon, and the recovery returns at a new address.
